newsitem.title: USA: Philip Morris ups stake in Mexico venture.
newsitem.headline: Philip Morris ups stake in Mexico venture.

text.p: Philip Morris International Inc said Friday that it and Mexico's Grupo Carso SA de CV had restructured their interests in their joint cigarette business in Mexico.

Philip Morris said under the agreement it would increase its equity interest in the business to 50 percent. The business is now being conducted by Cigarros La Tabacalera Mexicana SA de CV, or Cigatam.
A Philip Morris spokeswoman said the company's equity interest in the venture was 29 percent previously.
The company did not disclose financial details of its pact.
Cigatam has held the license to make and market certain Philip Morris brands, including Marlboro and Benson & Hedges since 1975.
As part of the pact, the license is being extended to the year 2020, Philip Morris said in a statement Friday evening.
The company said the pact remains subject to approval from Mexico's antitrust authority.
The announcement follows a $368.5 billion settlement reached a week ago between the tobacco companies and state attorneys general.
Philip Morris, the world's largest cigarette company, is expected to pay $6.5 billion of the initial payout, according to some reports.
Grupo Carso, one of the largest publicly-owned companies in Mexico, has holdings in construction, auto parts, consumer goods and retailing.
Philip Morris International is the tobacco operating company of Philip Morris Cos Inc, the world's largest consumer packaged goods company.
